data.summary: F10 stoppages are driven mainly by part shortages and AGV delays, with secondary torque faults on M-06 and andon triggers from missing parts and equipment issues.

findings.claim: Part shortages cause the most F10 downtime: supplier_short (high) has 22 incidents, 459.0 min downtime, 366 cars lost, while agv_down (medium) has 58 incidents, 171.9 min and agv_late (medium) has 29 incidents, 139.3 min.
Torque faults recur heavily at F10: controller_fault (medium) has 36 incidents and 451.7 min downtime, and torque_out_of_range (medium) has 37 incidents and 186.5 min downtime.
Andon events show missing_part is the top line-stop trigger at F10, with 97 stopped_line events in shift A averaging 186.3 s response and 97 linked incidents.
Equipment andon events also stop the F10 line in both shifts: 65 events in shift A and 66 events in shift B with stopped_line=true.
M-06 telemetry at F10 logs 47 failure rows, sometimes with overstrain_failure=1 and torque up to 76.6 nm, while heat_dissipation_failure stays 0.

data.recommendation: Prioritize resolving supplier_short part shortages and AGV delays at F10, then inspect M-06 torque controller and socket wear, since these causes account for the highest downtime and stopped-line andon events.
